simple: the PC's original interrupt controller chip, two of them chained.
analogy: the school secretary who decides which bell to pass on first.
precise: a programmable interrupt controller with eight request lines, an interrupt mask register (IMR), an interrupt request register (IRR) and an in-service register (ISR); the PC chains a slave to the master's line 2, giving 15 usable lines, and both must be remapped so their vectors do not overlap CPU exceptions.
source: D3 of F4-03 (Intel, "8259A Programmable Interrupt Controller" datasheet: initialisation command words, priority, end of interrupt, edge and level modes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: NVMe's one queue pair for management commands and the other queue pairs for reads and writes.
analogy: the office tray for contracts and the trays for everyday orders.
precise: queue 0 (admin), set up through the AQA, ASQ and ACQ registers and used for Identify, Set Features and queue creation; I/O queue pairs (1 and up) created by admin commands and used for NVM commands.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the standard way a computer talks to the chip that runs its SATA ports.
analogy: the logistics company's rule book for its loading dock.
precise: a register-level interface for SATA host bus adapters, found on PCI with class code 01h, subclass 06h, programming interface 01h; registers in a memory BAR (ABAR, BAR5), commands passed through per-port command lists in memory.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a register in which a device says how big a window of addresses it needs, and the firmware or OS writes where that window is.
analogy: "this visitor needs a room of this size"; the office writes in the room number.
precise: a configuration register at 0x10–0x24 (type 0 header) describing one I/O or memory region; low bits encode the type (I/O, 32-bit or 64-bit memory, prefetchable); the size is found by writing all ones and reading back which address bits are writable.
source: D1 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Base Address Registers", "Capabilities List")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: writing each decimal digit in its own 4 bits.
analogy: the clock's private code: one card per digit.
precise: an encoding in which a byte holds two decimal digits, the tens in bits 7–4 and the units in bits 3–0, so 45 is stored as 0x45; value = (byte >> 4) × 10 + (byte & 0xF).
source: D1 of F4-04 (Motorola, "MC146818 Real-Time Clock Plus RAM" datasheet (C3 reading): registers, format bits, update cycle, UIP, interrupts) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a recording of what a computer did, and when, while it started.
analogy: the timetable of the school's morning, minute by minute.
precise: a time-stamped log of boot events (on Windows an ETL trace, summarised per driver with init times and boot phases); in this course a table produced by the lab kernel from its own millisecond tick in QEMU, in the style of DRIVERS.html's driver lists.
source: D6 of F4-06 (This project's DRIVERS.html: List 1 (the test boot's driver table, row amdsata, and the note that init times alone do not explain a slow boot) and List 2 (storahci) (opened in this build; the project's own page)); R5 of F4-06 (R5 — lab run, step boottrace: boottrace.out, boottrace.csv, boottrace.log (two boots, healthy and slowahci; Listing 4)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: permission for a PCI device to read and write memory by itself.
analogy: the delivery truck's permit to drive onto the school grounds.
precise: bit 2 of the PCI command register; while it is clear, a device cannot start memory transactions, so no DMA happens and requests that need DMA never complete.
source: D5 of F4-05 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37): command register (bus master enable), capabilities list, vendor-specific capability ID) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the three numbers that address one PCI function, written bb:dd.f.
analogy: building, entrance, line in the book.
precise: an 8-bit bus number, a 5-bit device number and a 3-bit function number; a physical device may implement up to eight functions.
source: D1 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Base Address Registers", "Capabilities List")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a chain of optional feature descriptions inside configuration space.
analogy: extra pages stapled to the sign-in line: "also speaks sign language", "has a phone".
precise: a linked list starting at the pointer at offset 0x34 (when status bit 4 is set), each entry an ID byte and a next pointer; PCI Express adds an extended list at offset 0x100 with 16-bit IDs, reachable only through ECAM.
source: D1 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Base Address Registers", "Capabilities List")); D2 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Enhanced Configuration Access Mechanism", extended capabilities)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: three bytes that say what kind of device it is, regardless of who made it.
analogy: "here for: a lesson on mass storage".
precise: base class, subclass and programming interface at configuration offset 0x09–0x0B, for example 01.06.01 (mass storage, SATA, AHCI 1.0) or 01.08.02 (mass storage, non-volatile memory, NVM Express).
source: D1 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Base Address Registers", "Capabilities List")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number the driver puts on each command so it can recognise the answer.
analogy: the order number printed on the receipt.
precise: a 16-bit field in command dword 0, copied into the completion entry; unique among the commands outstanding on one SQ.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table of up to 32 commands a port can work on.
analogy: the 32 numbered bays.
precise: a 1 KiB-aligned array of 32-byte command headers at PxCLB; slot n is issued by setting bit n of PxCI and is finished when the HBA clears it.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a ring where the controller reports finished commands.
analogy: the receipt tray.
precise: a circular array of 16-byte entries (result, SQ head, SQ ID, command identifier, status with phase tag); the controller produces at the tail, the driver consumes at the head and reports it through the CQ head doorbell.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: resetting the SATA link and waiting for the disk to answer.
analogy: walking to a gate and shouting.
precise: an out-of-band reset signal the HBA sends when PxSCTL.DET is set to 1 and cleared again; a present device answers and the link comes up (PxSSTS.DET = 3); on an empty port nothing answers and only a timeout ends the wait.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)); D3 of F4-06 (SATA-IO, "Serial ATA" specification: out-of-band signalling, FIS types, the SStatus/SControl registers) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small block of registers every PCI device has, which describes the device and controls its basic behaviour.
analogy: the visitor's own line in the sign-in book.
precise: 256 bytes per function in conventional PCI (4096 bytes in PCI Express), starting with a standard header (vendor ID, device ID, command, status, class code, header type, BARs, capability pointer, interrupt line and pin).
source: D1 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Base Address Registers", "Capabilities List")); D2 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Enhanced Configuration Access Mechanism", extended capabilities)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one entry saying "here is a buffer, this long".
analogy: a delivery note naming a shelf and how much fits on it.
precise: a 16-byte entry: 64-bit physical address, 32-bit length, flags NEXT (another descriptor follows) and WRITE (the device writes this buffer), and the index of the next descriptor.
source: D1 of F4-05 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (curriculum item 38; C4 reading: "Basic Facilities of a Virtio Device", "Virtio Transport Options: Virtio Over PCI Bus", "Block Device", "Network Device")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of the kernel that knows how to talk to one kind of device.
analogy: an interpreter for a visitor who speaks another language.
precise: kernel code that owns a device's resources (register ranges, interrupt lines, DMA memory), implements a subsystem's interface (block, character, network, input) on top of the device's programming interface, and handles its errors and lifecycle.
source: D2 of F4-01 (Mark Russinovich, David Solomon, Alex Ionescu, Pavel Yosifovich, "Windows Internals", 7th edition, Part 1, chapter "I/O system" (curriculum item 30; C1 reading for the driver-model comparison): device objects, device stacks, Plug and Play, driver start types); D3 of F4-01 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (curriculum item 39; dated, concepts still useful): the device model, buses, drivers, probe and remove, platform devices) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a byte both sides use to record how far start-up has got.
analogy: the stamps on a supplier's contract: seen, assigned, terms agreed, active.
precise: a register in the common configuration with bits ACKNOWLEDGE (1), DRIVER (2), DRIVER_OK (4), FEATURES_OK (8), NEEDS_RESET (0x40) and FAILED (0x80); writing 0 resets the device.
source: D1 of F4-05 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (curriculum item 38; C4 reading: "Basic Facilities of a Virtio Device", "Virtio Transport Options: Virtio Over PCI Bus", "Block Device", "Network Device")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device reading or writing the computer's memory itself, without the CPU copying each byte.
analogy: the delivery truck driving the goods to the shelf.
precise: memory transactions started by a device (a PCI bus master) at addresses the driver gave it; the CPU only sets up the transfer and learns when it is done.
source: D4 of F4-05 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (curriculum item 39), chapter on memory mapping and DMA) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a register the driver writes to say "new orders up to here" or "I have read up to here".
analogy: the bells on the trays (not the faculty's doorbell analogy for interrupts, which ring the other way, from device to CPU).
precise: per queue, a tail doorbell for an SQ and a head doorbell for a CQ, at BAR0 offset 1000h + (2y or 2y + 1) × (4 << CAP.DSTRD).
source: D2 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVMe PCIe Transport Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: doorbells)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the kernel's rules for which driver serves which device.
analogy: the office's list of interpreters and the rule for assigning them.
precise: the data structures and procedures that record discovered devices, registered drivers and the bindings between them, and that call each driver's probe and remove at the right moments.
source: D2 of F4-01 (Mark Russinovich, David Solomon, Alex Ionescu, Pavel Yosifovich, "Windows Internals", 7th edition, Part 1, chapter "I/O system" (curriculum item 30; C1 reading for the driver-model comparison): device objects, device stacks, Plug and Play, driver start types); D3 of F4-01 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (curriculum item 39; dated, concepts still useful): the device model, buses, drivers, probe and remove, platform devices) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to read configuration space as ordinary memory.
analogy: a photocopy of every sign-in book laid out on one long table.
precise: the Enhanced Configuration Access Mechanism of PCI Express: a memory window in which each function's 4 KiB configuration space is at base + (bus << 20 | device << 15 | function << 12); its base and bus range come from the ACPI MCFG table.
source: D2 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Enhanced Configuration Access Mechanism", extended capabilities)); D3 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Firmware Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: MCFG)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the message a handler sends to the interrupt controller to say "I am done with this one".
analogy: telling the secretary "done" after answering the bell.
precise: a command (for the 8259, writing 0x20 to its command port) that clears the highest-priority in-service bit, allowing that line and lines of lower priority to be delivered again; slave lines need an EOI at both controllers.
source: D3 of F4-03 (Intel, "8259A Programmable Interrupt Controller" datasheet: initialisation command words, priority, end of interrupt, edge and level modes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number in an ACPI table saying which CMOS byte holds the century.
analogy: the note saying which drawer holds the century card.
precise: a one-byte field of the Fixed ACPI Description Table (signature "FACP") giving the CMOS RAM index of the century register; 0 means not supported.
source: D2 of F4-04 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum item 20; C3 reading: FADT century field)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: device and driver agreeing which optional abilities they will both use.
analogy: the supplier lists the services it can offer; the school ticks the ones it will use.
precise: the driver reads the device's 64 feature bits, writes back a subset it understands, and sets FEATURES_OK; the device confirms by keeping the bit set.
source: D1 of F4-05 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (curriculum item 38; C4 reading: "Basic Facilities of a Virtio Device", "Virtio Transport Options: Virtio Over PCI Bus", "Block Device", "Network Device")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many received bytes the UART collects before it rings.
analogy: the visitor waits until there are 14 words to say before pressing the bell.
precise: the 16550's receive FIFO raises the "received data available" interrupt when it holds at least the programmed number of bytes (1, 4, 8 or 14); a "character timeout" interrupt reports fewer bytes that have waited for a while.
source: D1 of F4-03 (National Semiconductor (now Texas Instruments), "PC16550D Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter with FIFOs" datasheet (C2 reading: interrupt enable and identification registers, FIFO control)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a packet on the SATA cable.
analogy: the company's printed forms.
precise: a typed frame exchanged between host and device; the driver builds register host-to-device FISes (type 27h) for commands and reads device-to-host FISes the HBA copies into the received-FIS area.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)); D3 of F4-06 (SATA-IO, "Serial ATA" specification: out-of-band signalling, FIS types, the SStatus/SControl registers) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the controller chip between the computer's bus and its disks.
analogy: the loading dock itself.
precise: the AHCI controller: global registers (CAP, GHC, IS, PI, VS) and up to 32 ports, each with its own register block.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the PC's keyboard and mouse controller.
analogy: a receptionist who collects the keyboard's and mouse's messages and passes them through one window.
precise: a controller with a data port (0x60) and a status/command port (0x64) that connects up to two PS/2 devices, raises line 1 for the keyboard and line 12 for the mouse, and can translate the keyboard's scan code set 2 into set 1.
source: D2 of F4-03 (OSDev wiki, pages "8042 PS/2 Controller", "PS/2 Keyboard", "PS/2 Mouse" (curriculum item 8; C2 reading)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the command that asks a disk to describe itself.
analogy: asking the visitor for an identity card.
precise: ATA command ECh, returning 256 16-bit words: serial number (words 10–19), firmware revision (23–26), model (27–46), the 48-bit sector count (100–103), and feature flags.
source: D2 of F4-06 (INCITS T13, "ATA/ATAPI Command Set" (ACS) (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: IDENTIFY DEVICE, READ/WRITE DMA EXT, FPDMA QUEUED; status and error registers)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a signal from a device that makes the CPU stop what it is doing and run a handler.
analogy: the doorbell a visitor rings at the school's front desk.
precise: an asynchronous event delivered to the CPU through an interrupt controller (here the 8259 PIC) that causes it to save state and run the handler registered for that line's vector; the handler acknowledges the device and the controller (EOI).
source: D3 of F4-03 (Intel, "8259A Programmable Interrupt Controller" datasheet: initialisation command words, priority, end of interrupt, edge and level modes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the layer that turns key presses into finished lines of text.
analogy: the interpreter writing a sentence, crossing out a wrong word, and handing it over only at the full stop.
precise: the TTY component that buffers input in canonical mode, applies editing characters (erase, kill), echoes, and delivers a line to the reader when a line terminator arrives.
source: D6 of F4-03 (The Open Group, "The Single UNIX Specification" (POSIX), General Terminal Interface: canonical mode input processing) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of device identities a driver says it can handle.
analogy: the languages an interpreter lists on the office board.
precise: an array of identifiers (PCI vendor/device IDs or class codes, ACPI or devicetree compatible strings) that the driver model compares with a device's identity before calling probe.
source: D3 of F4-01 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (curriculum item 39; dated, concepts still useful): the device model, buses, drivers, probe and remove, platform devices) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the firmware table that tells the OS where ECAM is.
analogy: the note saying which table the photocopies are on.
precise: an ACPI table (signature "MCFG") defined by the PCI Firmware Specification, listing for each PCI segment group the ECAM base address and the range of bus numbers it covers.
source: D3 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Firmware Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: MCFG)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a counter that only goes up, used to measure intervals.
analogy: the principal's stopwatch.
precise: a clock that never goes backwards and is not affected by setting the date; in the lab kernel, the count of PIT interrupts since boot (F4-03).
source: D4 of F4-04 (The Open Group, "The Single UNIX Specification" (POSIX), definitions of "Seconds Since the Epoch", CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one "disk" inside an NVMe controller.
analogy: one of the supplier's warehouses.
precise: a quantity of non-volatile memory addressed by logical blocks, with its own size and LBA format, identified by a namespace ID (NSID) that every I/O command names.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: letting a SATA disk hold up to 32 commands and finish them in the order it likes.
analogy: the dock clerk accepting a whole stack of orders and serving them in the most convenient order.
precise: the SATA mechanism using the FPDMA QUEUED commands (READ 60h, WRITE 61h) with a tag per command, PxSACT and Set Device Bits FISes to report completions; advertised by CAP.SNCQ on the HBA and in IDENTIFY data on the disk.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)); D2 of F4-06 (INCITS T13, "ATA/ATAPI Command Set" (ACS) (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: IDENTIFY DEVICE, READ/WRITE DMA EXT, FPDMA QUEUED; status and error registers)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the driver telling the device "look at the queue, there is new work".
analogy: phoning the depot.
precise: a write of the queue index to the queue's notify address, at notify-capability offset + queue_notify_off × notify_off_multiplier; also called a kick.
source: D1 of F4-05 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (curriculum item 38; C4 reading: "Basic Facilities of a Virtio Device", "Virtio Transport Options: Virtio Over PCI Bus", "Block Device", "Network Device")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the standard way a computer talks to fast flash SSDs on PCI Express.
analogy: the new supplier's tray system.
precise: a host controller interface with memory-resident submission and completion queues, doorbell registers, and admin and I/O command sets; on PCI, class code 010802h with registers in BAR0.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)); D2 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVMe PCIe Transport Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: doorbells)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device that connects a second PCI bus behind it.
analogy: a door to a second building with its own entrances.
precise: a function with a type 1 header holding primary, secondary and subordinate bus numbers and the address ranges it forwards; PCI Express root ports and switch ports appear to software as such bridges.
source: D1 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Base Address Registers", "Capabilities List")); D2 of F4-02 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 37; C1 reading: "Configuration Space", "Enhanced Configuration Access Mechanism", extended capabilities)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one bit in each completion that flips every time the controller goes round the queue.
analogy: this round's ink colour.
precise: bit 0 of the completion entry's status word; the controller writes the inverse of the previous value at that slot on each pass, starting from 1 on the first pass over a zeroed queue; an entry is new when its phase equals the phase the driver expects for the current pass.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device that cannot announce itself, so the kernel learns about it from a table or a convention.
analogy: a visitor written into the sign-in book in advance by someone else.
precise: a device at fixed addresses known from firmware tables (ACPI, devicetree) or platform convention (the PC's legacy I/O ports), as opposed to a device on a bus that can be enumerated, such as PCI.
source: D3 of F4-01 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (curriculum item 39; dated, concepts still useful): the device model, buses, drivers, probe and remove, platform devices) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: x86's separate small address space for devices, reached with special instructions.
analogy: the internal phone numbers of the school, separate from street addresses.
precise: a 64 Ki-entry I/O address space accessed with the IN and OUT instructions; legacy PC devices such as the 16550 UART at 0x3F8 live there (F1-41).
source: D5 of F4-01 (Intel Corporation, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 1, chapter on input/output (I/O port address space, IN/OUT) (curriculum item 10)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one "put this many bytes here" entry for a command's data.
analogy: one shelf on the order's shelf list.
precise: a 16-byte entry of the command table's PRD table: data base address and a byte count minus one (bit 0 must give an even count); a command's data is the concatenation of its PRDs.
source: D1 of F4-06 (Intel, "Serial ATA Advanced Host Controller Interface (AHCI)" specification (curriculum item 41; C5 reading: HBA memory registers, port registers, command list, received FIS, command table, "Software Manipulation of Port DMA Engines", initialization chapter)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the driver's first contact with a device it might serve; it may say no.
analogy: the interpreter's first greeting.
precise: a driver callback invoked when a device matches one of the driver's IDs; it checks the device, acquires its resources, initialises it and returns success (the driver now owns the device) or an error (the device stays unbound).
source: D3 of F4-01 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (curriculum item 39; dated, concepts still useful): the device model, buses, drivers, probe and remove, platform devices) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a pointer to one memory page of a command's data.
analogy: a shelf number on the order.
precise: a 64-bit physical address; a command carries PRP1 and PRP2; for data spanning more than two pages, PRP2 points to a page-aligned list of further PRP entries.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small clock chip that keeps the date and time even when the computer is off.
analogy: the battery clock in the entrance hall.
precise: a battery-backed counter of seconds, minutes, hours, day, month and year, on PCs compatible with the Motorola MC146818 and reached through CMOS index port 0x70 and data port 0x71.
source: D1 of F4-04 (Motorola, "MC146818 Real-Time Clock Plus RAM" datasheet (C3 reading): registers, format bits, update cycle, UIP, interrupts) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of a device's control and status boxes and where each one is.
analogy: the visitor's phrasebook: which word means what.
precise: the offsets, widths, reset values, field layouts and access rules (read-only, write-only, read/write, write-1-to-clear) of a device's registers, as given by its specification or datasheet.
source: D1 of F4-01 (National Semiconductor (now Texas Instruments), "PC16550D Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter with FIFOs" datasheet (curriculum C2 reading): register description, divisor latch, line status, modem control loopback, scratch register) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a circular queue where one side only writes and the other side only reads.
analogy: the interpreter's notebook, written by one hand and read by another.
precise: a fixed array with a producer index and a consumer index, each written by only one party; with one producer and one consumer it needs no lock, only the right ordering of the data write before the index update.
source: D5 of F4-03 (Anthony Williams, "C++ Concurrency in Action" (curriculum item 3): single-producer, single-consumer queues and memory ordering) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number a keyboard sends for a key going down or coming up.
analogy: the key's seat number, not its letter.
precise: a byte sequence identifying a key position and a make (press) or break (release) event; in set 1 a break is the make code with bit 7 set, in set 2 a break is 0xF0 followed by the make code.
source: D2 of F4-03 (OSDev wiki, pages "8042 PS/2 Controller", "PS/2 Keyboard", "PS/2 Mouse" (curriculum item 8; C2 reading)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a ring of commands the driver writes for the controller.
analogy: the order tray.
precise: a circular array of 64-byte entries in host memory; the driver owns the tail and advances it by writing the SQ tail doorbell; the controller consumes from the head.
source: D1 of F4-07 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 42; C6 reading: controller registers, admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue; queue mechanics, phase tag)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number of seconds since the start of 1970 (UTC), ignoring leap seconds.
analogy: the school counting every second since its founding day, instead of using a calendar.
precise: seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z computed as days × 86400 + seconds of the day, where every day has exactly 86400 seconds.
source: D4 of F4-04 (The Open Group, "The Single UNIX Specification" (POSIX), definitions of "Seconds Since the Epoch", CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a flag that warns the clock is about to change its numbers.
analogy: a light that comes on just before the cards flip.
precise: bit 7 of RTC status register A; while it is set, an update cycle is imminent or running and the time registers may be inconsistent.
source: D1 of F4-04 (Motorola, "MC146818 Real-Time Clock Plus RAM" datasheet (C3 reading): registers, format bits, update cycle, UIP, interrupts) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a standard format for packing files into one archive, used by tar.
analogy: a box of files with a label on top of each one.
precise: the POSIX ustar interchange format: a 512-byte header per entry (name, octal size, type, checksum, the magic "ustar"), data padded to 512 bytes, and two zero blocks at the end; the lab's read-only root file system.
source: D5 of F4-07 (IEEE Std 1003.1 (POSIX), pax utility, "ustar Interchange Format"); R5 of F4-07 (R5 — lab run, step root: root.out, root.log (Listing 5's expected lines against the kernel's)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a family of devices designed for virtual machines, with one shared way of talking to all of them.
analogy: suppliers who all accept the same order form.
precise: the OASIS "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" standard: common device status and feature negotiation, virtqueues for data, and transports (PCI, MMIO, channel I/O) that carry them.
source: D1 of F4-05 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (curriculum item 38; C4 reading: "Basic Facilities of a Virtio Device", "Virtio Transport Options: Virtio Over PCI Bus", "Block Device", "Network Device")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the queue in shared memory through which a driver hands buffers to a virtio device and gets them back.
analogy: the order board plus the receipt book.
precise: in the split layout, a descriptor table, an available ring written by the driver and a used ring written by the device.
source: D1 of F4-05 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (curriculum item 38; C4 reading: "Basic Facilities of a Virtio Device", "Virtio Transport Options: Virtio Over PCI Bus", "Block Device", "Network Device")) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time people read on a clock: date and time of day.
analogy: what the hall clock shows.
precise: a time scale tied to civil time (here UTC), which can be set and can jump; contrasted with a monotonic clock, which only moves forward at a steady rate from an arbitrary start.
source: D4 of F4-04 (The Open Group, "The Single UNIX Specification" (POSIX), definitions of "Seconds Since the Epoch", CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a status bit you switch off by writing a 1 to it.
analogy: pressing the lit button on a call panel to say "seen".
precise: an access rule in which writing 1 to a bit clears it and writing 0 leaves it unchanged, so software can acknowledge some events without losing others that arrived meanwhile.
source: D4 of F4-01 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" and "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum item 37): register attribute conventions including write-1-to-clear status bits) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
